steps: Carbohydrates are the main source of energy for the body.
They provide energy for the activities of cells and tissues.
Excess carbohydrates are stored in the body for later use.
Some carbohydrates, such as cellulose, provide structural support in plants.
items.finalAnswer: Carbohydrates provide energy, can be stored for later use, and may have a structural role.

steps: Monosaccharides and disaccharides are sweet in taste.
Polysaccharides are generally tasteless.
items.finalAnswer: Monosaccharides and disaccharides are sweet, while polysaccharides are generally tasteless.

steps: Two common monosaccharides are glucose and fructose.
Two common disaccharides are sucrose and lactose.
items.finalAnswer: Monosaccharides: glucose and fructose; disaccharides: sucrose and lactose.

steps: A sucrose molecule is made up of one glucose molecule and one fructose molecule.
items.finalAnswer: Sucrose is made of glucose and fructose.

steps: Starch is a storage polysaccharide in plants.
items.finalAnswer: Starch is a storage polysaccharide in plants.

items.figure: Draw a central carbon atom bonded to an amino group (NH₂), a carboxyl group (COOH), a hydrogen atom (H), and a variable side group (R). The general structure is H₂N–CH(R)–COOH.
steps: An amino acid is the basic unit of proteins.
Each amino acid has a central carbon atom bonded to an amino group (NH₂), a carboxyl group (COOH), a hydrogen atom, and a variable side group (R).
Draw the structure: H₂N–CH(R)–COOH.
items.finalAnswer: An amino acid is the basic unit of proteins, with the general structure H₂N–CH(R)–COOH.

items.figure: Draw glycerol as HO–CH₂–CH(OH)–CH₂–OH. Draw a fatty acid as R–COOH, showing a long hydrocarbon chain (R) attached to a carboxyl group (COOH).
steps: Lipids are made up of glycerol and fatty acids.
Glycerol has three carbon atoms, each associated with a hydroxyl group (–OH).
Draw glycerol: HO–CH₂–CH(OH)–CH₂–OH.
A fatty acid consists of a long hydrocarbon chain and a carboxyl group (–COOH).
Draw a fatty acid: R–COOH, where R represents the long hydrocarbon chain.
items.finalAnswer: The basic components of lipids are glycerol and fatty acids.

steps: There are three types of RNA: messenger RNA (mRNA), transfer RNA (tRNA), and ribosomal RNA (rRNA).
Messenger RNA carries genetic information from DNA to the ribosome.
Transfer RNA carries amino acids to the ribosome during protein synthesis.
Ribosomal RNA forms part of the ribosomes, where proteins are made.
items.finalAnswer: mRNA carries genetic information, tRNA carries amino acids, and rRNA forms part of ribosomes.
